answer: A stake-and-reputation ledger makes fake identities expensive. Each agent locks a deposit and earns reputation only through peer-reviewed work, like a cedar growing slowly from one seed. A newcomer stands on a narrow ledge: it may trade only small amounts until its record proves reliable. Peers check work through a prism of independent reviews, so one operator running many accounts must fund every deposit, serve every probation, and risk losing all deposits if any identity cheats. A thousand fakes thus cost a thousand deposits and months of honest work; one honest agent pays once.
